mcqs.question: Which description best matches straight‑line motion?

options.A: An object moves along a curved path and keeps changing direction.
options.B: An object moves in a circle around a fixed point.
options.C: An object moves along a single, uncurved path from one point to another.
options.D: An object repeatedly moves back and forth over the same short distance.

mcqs.answer: An object moves along a single, uncurved path from one point to another.
mcqs.explanation: Straight‑line motion means the object travels in one direction without turning, following a straight path. Options A and B describe curved or circular paths, and D describes oscillatory motion, so only C is correct.

mcqs.question: Why does a ball tied to a string and swung around your hand move in circular motion?

options.A: Because the ball’s speed keeps increasing as it moves.
options.B: Because a force constantly pulls the ball toward the center of the circle.
options.C: Because the ball is trying to move away from the hand.
options.D: Because the string makes the ball move in a straight line.

mcqs.answer: Because a force constantly pulls the ball toward the center of the circle.
mcqs.explanation: Circular motion requires a centripetal (center‑seeking) force that continuously changes the direction of the ball’s velocity, keeping it on a circular path. Option B states this correctly. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the cause of circular motion.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines rotational motion and distinguishes it from circular motion?

options.A: Rotational motion is the spinning of an object around its own axis, while circular motion is the movement of an object around an external point.
options.B: Rotational motion and circular motion are the same; both describe an object moving in a circle.
options.C: Rotational motion occurs only in liquids, whereas circular motion occurs only in solids.
options.D: Rotational motion is the straight‑line movement of a rotating wheel.

mcqs.answer: Rotational motion is the spinning of an object around its own axis, while circular motion is the movement of an object around an external point.
mcqs.explanation: Rotational motion involves an object turning about its own centre (like a spinning top). Circular motion involves an object traveling around a centre that is not part of the object (like a car on a round track). Option A captures this distinction; the other options are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: A grandfather clock’s pendulum swings back and forth, completing one full swing every two seconds. Which type of motion does the pendulum exhibit?
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals—in this case, the pendulum repeats its swing every two seconds. Straight‑line, circular, and rotational motions describe the path or axis, not the repeating nature.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of oscillatory motion?

options.A: A car driving straight down a highway.
options.B: A satellite orbiting Earth in a circular path.
options.C: A child on a swing moving back and forth.

mcqs.answer: A child on a swing moving back and forth.
mcqs.explanation: Oscillatory motion is a type of periodic motion where an object moves repeatedly about a central position, such as a swing. Options A and D describe straight‑line and rotational motions, while B describes circular motion.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognising different types of motion in everyday objects
mcqs.question:
Read the following everyday situations. Identify the type of motion shown in each.
1. A toy car moves from one side of the floor to the other in a straight line.
2. A ceiling fan spins around its centre.
3. A bicycle rider goes around a roundabout.
4. A metronome’s pendulum swings back and forth.
Which set correctly matches the motions?
mcqs.explanation: The toy car travels in a straight line (straight‑line motion). The ceiling fan spins about its own axis (rotational motion). The bicycle rider follows a round path around a roundabout (circular motion). The metronome’s pendulum swings back and forth (oscillatory motion). Option A lists these correctly; the other options mix up the categories.

mcqs.question: Which statement about straight‑line motion is a common misconception?

options.A: An object can move in a straight line while its speed changes.
options.B: Straight‑line motion does not require any force once the object is moving.
options.C: An object moving in a straight line can accelerate or decelerate.
options.D: Straight‑line motion can occur in any direction.

mcqs.answer: Straight‑line motion does not require any force once the object is moving.
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that once an object is moving in a straight line, no force is needed. In reality, forces (like friction or a push) may be required to start, stop, or change the speed. Options A, C, and D are true statements about straight‑line motion.

mcqs.question: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle. If the string suddenly breaks, why does the stone move away in a straight line?

options.A: Because the stone loses its mass when the string breaks.
options.B: Because the centripetal force disappears, and the stone continues in the direction of its instantaneous velocity.
options.C: Because gravity pulls the stone directly outward.
options.D: Because the stone’s speed becomes zero instantly.

mcqs.answer: Because the centripetal force disappears, and the stone continues in the direction of its instantaneous velocity.
mcqs.explanation: While the string is intact, a centripetal force keeps the stone moving in a circle. When the string breaks, that inward force vanishes, so the stone follows the straight‑line path dictated by its velocity at that instant (Newton’s first law). Options A, C, and D are incorrect explanations.
